function.name: get_stock_price
function.description: Get the closing stock price for a specific company on a specified date. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

date.description: Date of when to get the stock price. Format: yyyy-mm-dd.

exchange.description: Name of the stock exchange market where the company's stock is listed. Default is 'NASDAQ'

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "2022-01-01 and 2022-02-01 在 Nasdaq 的 Microsoft 和 Apple 收盘价是多少?" They want closing prices for those dates.

We need to call the tool twice per company? Actually we can do four calls: two companies (Microsoft, Apple) times two dates each. The function signature requires company name, date, optional exchange default NASDAQ. So we will make separate calls:

1. get_stock_price(company_name="Microsoft", date="2022-01-01")
2. get_stock_price(company_name="Apple", date="2022-01-01")
3. get_stock_price(company_name="Microsoft", date="2022-02-01")
4. get_stock_price(company_name="Apple", date="2022-02-01")

But note: On Jan 1st 2022 was New Year's Day; markets were closed. We might have no data or maybe use previous trading day close. But the question likely expects us to provide actual closing prices if available. For Jan 1, there would be no trading because it's holiday. Might return null or error. We'll see what the API returns.
